campaigns.title: USD/JPY — MTF signal engine
campaigns.dataset: Dukascopy 1-min · walk-forward 14-day slices · M5+M15+M30+H1 pooled · single account · risk 1%/trade
campaigns.headline: Entry timing IS the edge. Same signals: PF 0.65 (late) → 0.81 (break) → 1.92 (on-time). Master detect.js constant across every trial.
findings: Entry timing dominates — moving only the entry took the identical 2-year edge from PF 0.65 to 1.92.
Erik's break-of-prior-low entry beats the late confirm entry in every pairing; at TF resolution it's ~breakeven (needs the 1m to be early).
Erik's exhaustion-candle exit lifts win rate (to ~40–60%); 2R target gives the highest profit factor.
Spread is survivable — the target config keeps PF 1.92 with full 1.3p cost. Optimize entry, not cost.

campaigns.title: 1m Gate Executor (LIVE-ready)
campaigns.dataset: Higher-TF (M15/M30) arms the setup, 1m state machine: 9/20 converge -> 20MA break -> prior-swing break = IN, exhaust-candle exit, single account, spread, rollover blocked, risk 1%/trade, NO look-ahead
campaigns.headline: The honest translation WORKS — and the account grows on EXPECTANCY, not profit factor. Letting winners run (2R) beats bailing early (exhaust) even with a lower PF. Sizing is the multiplier (see Scaling tab).
findings: First honest, no-look-ahead config that MAKES MONEY. Every timeframe-level version lost (PF 0.65-0.81). The 1m entry precision is the whole difference.
PF and win% do NOT grow the account — EXPECTANCY (R/trade) does. Exhaust exit: 65% win but +0.19R (small wins). 2R target: 53% win, +0.39R — nearly 2x the balance at the same risk.
Trailing the 9EMA on the 1m is WORSE (+0.17R) — the minute 9EMA is too choppy and kicks you out of runners. A fixed R target is the better ‘let it run’.
Out-of-sample by year (2R): 2023-24 and 2024-25 both profitable independently. Then sizing multiplies it — see the Scaling tab.

campaigns.title: 3-Pair Portfolio (EUR/USD + USD/JPY + XAU/USD)
campaigns.dataset: The honest 1m gate executor (2R exit) run on EUR/USD, USD/JPY and XAU/USD, pooled onto ONE $1000 account, ONE position at a time across all three. Per-instrument pip + spread. Risk 1%/trade. Solo rows = each pair on its own account; pooled = the portfolio.
campaigns.headline: Breadth delivers near-daily cadence (89% of weekdays). Three pairs pooled, honest gold spread (4.6p): PF 1.64, 23/25 green months, 10% drawdown, $1k→$7.5k at 1% risk over 2 years.
findings: 89% of weekdays have a trade (2.7 on an active day) — breadth turns the selective single-pair engine into a near-daily one, exactly as expected.
All three pairs profitable solo. Pooled PF 1.64 with the corrected gold spread (4.6p, was 3.0). Gold is the thinnest edge — its wide spread eats into it.
Sized to the sweet spot: 2% → $82k (17% DD), 3% → $651k (26% DD) over 2 years. 5%+ is uncapped compounding — the 100-lot cap would throttle the top.
Honest throughout: no look-ahead, spread in, one position at a time. This is the portfolio the demo forward-test should mirror.

campaigns.title: ★ 3% Triplet Scale-out (flagship)
campaigns.dataset: Position-structure test on the honest 3-pair edge: 1 unit vs 2 vs 3, identical vs scale-out (bank one at the target, run the rest). Real per-order 100-lot cap, 3% risk per unit. Equity curves are the actual historical path; ruin/median from 5,000 Monte-Carlo shuffles.
campaigns.headline: NEW FLAGSHIP: 3% triplet scale-out (bank 1 at target, run 2). MC median $4.5M / 2yr, 0% ruin in 5,000 shuffles — beats every doublet on money AND drawdown. Three smaller units each get their own 100-lot ceiling (300 total) and two ride the trend tail.
campaigns.note: ★ 3% Triplet — bank 1, run 2. MC: 0% ruin in 5,000 shuffles, ~$4.5M median. Beats the 5% doublet on money AND drawdown. (Equity shown is the actual historical path — a rougher ~73% DD; the 5,000-shuffle average DD is ~52%.)
findings: Each added unit gets its OWN 100-lot ceiling — 3 units = 300 lots of capacity vs 200 (doublet) vs 100 (single). That headroom is the engine of the gain at scale.
Scale-out beats identical at every level: the runner units capture 1.18x per trade by riding the trend tail past the target.
3% triplet scale-out: MC median ~$4.5M, 0% ruin, avg DD ~52% — more money AND lower drawdown than the 5% doublet ($3.1M). The efficient frontier.
⚠ LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION: this assumes the broker 100-lot cap is PER-ORDER. If it is a TOTAL-account cap, 3 units share 100 and the triplet edge vanishes — confirm with the broker.
Honest DD: the actual historical path drew down ~73% (rougher than the 52% shuffle-average). Zero blow-ups, but a brutal ride at 9% total risk.

campaigns.title: ★ 1x9 — the flagship
campaigns.dataset: Same FIXED 9% total risk, split across N units (1 banks at target + N-1 run). Per-order 100-lot cap means N units = N×100 lots of capacity. Equity curves = actual historical path; ruin/median from 3,000 Monte-Carlo shuffles.
campaigns.headline: 1x9: nine units at 1% each (bank 1, run 8). Same 9% total risk as any split here — but 900 lots of capacity. MC median $12.9M/2yr, worst-of-3000 $9.7M, 0% ruin. The shape is the edge; the units are the volume — every N-split curve is the same shape, only the scale changes.
campaigns.note: ★ 1x9 — the flagship. 9 units × 1%. MC: 0% ruin, median ~$12.9M, worst-of-3000 ~$9.7M. Same 9% total risk as one unit, 9× the lot capacity. (Equity = actual path ~74% DD; shuffle-avg ~54%.)
findings: Erik was RIGHT: at a FIXED total risk, more (smaller) units = more money at the SAME ruin. Ruin stays ~0% at every split (total risk unchanged); only capacity grows.
1%×9 = 900 lots of capacity, MC median $12.9M, and even the WORST of 3,000 shuffles made ~$9.7M — robust, not a lucky path.
The real ceiling is no longer risk — it is the broker: max concurrent open positions + margin for N×100 lots. CONFIRM your broker allows 9+ positions.
Honest ride: ~54% shuffle-avg drawdown (historical path ~74%). Zero blow-ups, but you WILL be down ~half at some point — that is the cost, not ruin.
5% single unit (36% DD, one order) remains the simple/calm alternative. 1%×9 is max return at the same ruin, for 9 orders and a rougher ride.

campaigns.title: 3-Pair Detail (trade log + breakdowns)
campaigns.dataset: Every trade the pooled 3-pair executor took over 2 years, plus per-pair and exit-reason breakdowns. Same engine as the portfolio tab.
campaigns.headline: 1249 trades across EUR/USD, USD/JPY and XAU/USD (honest gold spread 4.6p). ~80% exit on the 9EMA-flip (ride the trend till it breaks), rest on the 2R target or stop. Full log below.
mechanism: ARM (M15/M30, detect.js): price stretched to a Bollinger band AT a level, in a climax — sets direction, says watch. No trade yet.
ENTRY (1-minute gate machine): 9/20 MA converge → price breaks the 20MA → price breaks the prior swing = IN.
EXIT: 2R target, OR stop at the swing against you, OR a decisive 9EMA break (2 closes through) — whichever hits first.
SIZE: risk 1% of balance per trade, ONE position at a time across all three pairs. Identical code in backtest + live alerts.

campaigns.title: Risk Ladder — uncapped (theoretical)
campaigns.dataset: The honest 3-pair edge compounded at each risk %, R-based with NO broker lot cap. This is the pure theoretical compounding — the ‘fantasy’ curves. The real cap-limited numbers are on the Ceiling Finder tab.
campaigns.headline: Uncapped theoretical compounding: 1% $7.5k → 2% $52k → 3% $322k → 5% $9.5M → 7% $195M. NO lot cap modeled — the broker’s 100-lot ceiling throttles the top hard (see Ceiling tab). Fun to look at; not the live number.
findings: R-based compounding, no lot cap — assumes you can always place the lots the risk % calls for. Above ~$150k balance that breaks (see Ceiling Finder).
Realistic zone (2-3%): $52k-$322k over 2 years — here the cap barely binds, so these ARE close to real.
5%+ ($9.5M, $195M) is the pure math with no broker limit — the fantasy. The Ceiling Finder shows what the 100-lot cap actually allows.
Every rung is the SAME honest edge (PF 1.64, spread in) — only the sizing changes.

campaigns.title: Ceiling Finder (real 100-lot cap)
campaigns.dataset: The honest 3-pair edge sized with REAL lot mechanics: lots capped at the broker max of 100, real per-pair pip values (EUR $10, gold $10, yen ~$6.4). Risk pushed to the breaking point to find the true max.
campaigns.headline: The system’s TRUE mathematical ceiling over 2 years from $1k: ~$1.84M at an absurd 65% risk (66% DD, 98% lot-capped). The 100-lot cap turns the $195M fantasy into a bounded ~$1.8M. Everything meaningful lives at 3-5%.
findings: The 100-lot cap bends the exponential into a plateau: 5% $990k, 15% $1.6M, and it TOPS OUT ~$1.84M no matter how hard you push.
The cap doesn’t bind until ~$150k balance — so from $300 up to six figures, the compounding is real and uncapped.
Past 5% it’s brutal diminishing returns: you 2x the money from 5%→ceiling but the drawdown goes from 45% to 66%+ and 98% of trades hit the cap.
Practical max for a human: 3-5% ($322k-$990k) captures most of the achievable money at a drawdown you could theoretically survive. The rest is math, not tradeable.
